title: What a $5,000 Raise Really Adds per Paycheck

scenes.say: A $5,000 raise added only about $126 to Darius's paycheck.
He's in the 22% bracket, so taxes take a real bite first.
That leaves roughly $3,270 a year, split over 26 paychecks.
And $126 disappears fast if nothing has a job.
So Darius splits it before it ever hits checking. Half to savings, half to spend.
That's about $1,640 saved in the first year, without feeling poorer.
His checklist: know the net number, automate the split, enjoy the rest.
Do you know your raise after tax? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because a $5,000 raise can mean $126 a paycheck.

description: Darius got a $5,000 raise, but after federal tax at 22%, Social Security, Medicare and state tax it adds only about $126 per paycheck. He splits it before it hits checking and saves roughly $1,640 in the first year. Numbers are rounded US estimates and tax depends on your situation.
